# Surface scaffolds

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:surface-scaffold` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

Typed Web Awesome dialog preferred widths and viewport bounds, presentation, and popup inset composition.

## When to use

Configure recurring dialog and popup geometry without consumer ::part() overrides.

- A Web Awesome dialog or dropdown needs a standard size, presentation, body/footer inset, or list-compatible menu inset.
- A dialog body should compose rows, sections, or aligned bare prose through List and ListInsetText.
- A modal needs a typed preferred width, viewport gutter, or dynamic viewport-bounded height cap while retaining native body scrolling and footer actions.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it as a generic layout wrapper or to replace application-owned modal state and focus lifecycle.
- Do not stack a dialog body inset around children that already own List or content-item geometry; use bodyInset none.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/surface-scaffold` — exports `DialogSurface`, `PopupSurface`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/surface-scaffold` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/surface-scaffold.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Registration: import `@kerfjs/ui/surface-scaffold/register` once (a side effect).
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css, custom-element-registration.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/surface-scaffold`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuisurface-scaffold) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- small, medium, or large dialog
- modal, side-sheet, or fullscreen dialog
- typed modal preferred width, viewport gutter, and maximum height, including viewport cap
- none, compact, or comfortable body and footer inset
- standard, compact, or zero-inset popup menu

**CSS-value props** (typed builders from `@kerfjs/ui/css-values`; raw CSS strings are rejected):

- `preferredWidth`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; helpers `px`, `rem`, `remify`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `preferredWidth={remify(832)}`
- `viewportGutter`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; helpers `px`, `rem`, `remify`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `viewportGutter={remify(8)}`
- `maxHeight`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; shorthands `viewport`; helpers `px`, `rem`, `remify`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `maxHeight="viewport"`

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [Dialog](./wa-dialog.md), [Dropdown](./wa-dropdown.md), [Dropdown Item](./wa-dropdown-item.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** open state; focus lifecycle; dismissal policy; content; outer placement.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: parent · border: child · padding: self (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

## Accessibility

- Supply the wrapped wa-dialog label and retain Web Awesome's native modal and focus behavior.
- Use popup surfaces only for real dropdown menus with named triggers.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-dialog-surface`, `kui-popup-surface`.

Never put `kui-dialog-surface` on an element you write; render `DialogSurface` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Never put `kui-popup-surface` on an element you write; render `PopupSurface` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Public tokens it reads: `--kui-radius-l`, `--kui-wa-container-inset`, `--kui-wa-surface-inset`. Set a token only where its public contract allows; prefer a prop.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
